request: Find three organizations in New York that support mental health awareness and community belonging, and draft partnership inquiries.
philosophy: Be somebody who makes everybody feel like somebody.

recommendation.headline: Prioritize HALI and NYC Health’s Clubhouses; qualify IDHA’s New York availability before advancing
recommendation.recommendation: Pursue exploratory inquiries to Hands Across Long Island (HALI) and NYC Health’s Clubhouses first. HALI’s peer-led mental-health services and concrete community supports provide a practical basis for discussing current needs. Clubhouses offer explicit alignment with dignity, member contribution, mental-health support, and community connection, but require identifying an individual clubhouse partner. Retain the selected Institute for the Development of Human Arts (IDHA) inquiry as a qualification step: its mental-health education aligns with the mission, while New York delivery and substantive belonging activities remain unconfirmed. These are potential leads, not existing relationships or commitments.
rationale: Charitable alignment: HALI combines peer-led mental-health support with community services, including a food pantry and clothing closet. Clubhouses support New Yorkers with serious mental health conditions in pursuing their chosen goals. IDHA provides mental-health education, events, and resources.

Philosophical alignment: Clubhouses provide the clearest explicit evidence for helping people feel seen and valued through dignity and member contribution. HALI’s peer-led services and community participation activities support human connection. IDHA’s practical contribution to belonging remains unclear.

Practical feasibility: The drafts ask for contacts, requirements, and current needs rather than proposing a funded activity or volunteer commitment. HALI has established Long Island geography; Clubhouses have established New York City geography. IDHA needs a local-availability check.

Evidence quality: Mission Discovery reports checked sources for all selected leads. Source verification does not establish partnership availability, program outcomes, accessibility, or collaboration terms.

Selection limitation: The code-selected shortlist differs from Mission Discovery’s preferred local leads, which included NAMI-NYC rather than IDHA. The selected set does not yet establish three individual New York organizational partners.

risks: The selected shortlist falls short of confirming three individual New York organizations: Clubhouses is a network, and IDHA’s New York availability is not established.
Partnership costs, current availability, outside-volunteer requirements, participant interest, and collaboration terms are unknown. No dates are confirmed.
IDHA’s search snippet describes connection and shared learning, but the supplied excerpt does not substantiate those activities.
HALI’s claim to be Long Island’s only peer-run mental-health organization is not independently established. Dates in its source metadata do not establish actionable opportunities.
No source is reported as flagged for instruction-like text. Underlying source text is not included here for an independent assessment.
decisions_for_board: Decide whether a designated person should send the HALI exploratory inquiry and Clubhouses referral inquiry after confirming recipient contacts.
Decide whether to send IDHA’s qualification inquiry now or hold it pending confirmation of New York availability.
Choose the human sender and signatory, and review the actual draft wording before sending. Keep all inquiries explicitly exploratory, without funding, volunteer, or scheduling commitments.
Decide whether to revisit NAMI-NYC if three confirmed New York organizations remain the priority.
next_steps: Review and edit the unsent drafts in Partnerships & Outreach; confirm each recipient’s appropriate contact.
For HALI, ask which current needs and participant-preferred activities could appropriately involve an outside foundation.
For Clubhouses, request an individual clubhouse referral and confirm member interest before developing an activity.
For IDHA, establish New York delivery, intended audiences, accessibility, and event-proposal requirements before discussing a collaboration format.
Bring any replies back to the board with confirmed scope, costs, requirements, and open questions. A person would send any approved inquiry outside SAM SPACE.
lessons_applied: Compassion and kindness were assessed through practical services and support for people’s chosen goals, not assumed emotional impact.
Human connection and helping people feel valued favored peer-led and member-directed approaches, consistent with “Be somebody who makes everybody feel like somebody.”
Mental-health awareness and support provide the strongest shared mission alignment. Eating-disorder-specific alignment is unclear for every candidate.
Welcoming people regardless of background, ability, or circumstance is unclear from the supplied evidence; accessibility and eligibility need confirmation.
Community activities support exploration, but sustained community-building outcomes are not established.
caveats: Every draft is unsent. A person must review it and send it outside SAM SPACE if the board agrees.
The input labels the research as live; it does not identify the data as synthetic. This packet relies only on the supplied specialist results and does not independently verify them.
No source URLs or recipient contact details were supplied here. Mission Discovery reports fetching five of six sources; MHANYS’s source was unreachable with HTTP 403.

NAMI-NYC merits a second look because its New York mental-health support and peer-connection evidence is clear. Its Possible fit label reflects a prohibition on observing support groups; a public-education inquiry is the appropriate alternative.

Belong Center remains exploratory because New York delivery and program details are unconfirmed, and its evidence-based claim lacks supporting studies in the excerpt. MHANYS needs reachable organizational evidence before advancement.
Only draft subjects, purposes, and next steps are included in this packet’s input, not full message bodies. Nothing has been sent, agreed, scheduled, or committed.

drafts.opportunity: Explore collaboration with an individual clubhouse on member-directed community activities, subject to member interest and outside-partner requirements.
drafts.body:
Hello NYC Health Clubhouses team,

I’m writing on behalf of the Sabrina Audrey Milone Foundation (Smile Like Sab), established in memory of Sabrina Audrey Milone. Our focus includes mental health awareness, eating disorder research and support, and community-building initiatives.

Your clubhouse program’s purpose—enriching the lives of New Yorkers with serious mental health conditions and empowering them to reach their chosen life goals—resonates with our community-building focus. We are particularly interested in the model’s emphasis on dignity, belonging, and member contribution.

We would like to explore whether a member-directed community activity could be useful to an individual clubhouse, with members’ interests guiding any discussion. We have not identified a clubhouse partner, and outside-partner requirements, costs, and scheduling remain unknown.

Could you direct us to an appropriate clubhouse contact who might be open to an initial discussion and explain the requirements for outside partners?

Thank you for your guidance.

Warm regards,

Sabrina Audrey Milone Foundation

[Phone]

Hello HALI team,

I’m writing on behalf of the Sabrina Audrey Milone Foundation (Smile Like Sab), established in memory of Sabrina Audrey Milone. Our focus includes mental health awareness, eating disorder research and support, and community-building initiatives.

HALI’s peer-run mental-health approach on Long Island, community engagement, and attention to social determinants of health resonate with our mission. We would like to learn whether there is a useful, participant-informed way to explore collaboration.

Possible areas for discussion include community participation or Creative Connections activities, or whether your food pantry or clothing closet accepts foundation-organized contributions. We would want to understand current needs and participant preferences before developing any proposal. Acceptance policies, volunteer requirements, costs, and scheduling are not yet known to us.

Could you connect us with the person who handles community partnerships for a brief exploratory conversation?

Thank you for your guidance and consideration.

Warm regards,
